children: The company recorded 21 per cent volume growth, with festive demand supporting decorative paints and infrastructure, energy and automotive sectors driving industrial coatings

JSW Dulux reported revenue from operations of Rs 961.9 crore in the second quarter of FY27, registering a 21.3 per cent increase over Rs 793.3 crore in the corresponding period last year on a comparable retained-business basis. Volume grew 21 per cent, supported by demand across its decorative and industrial paints businesses.

The company’s performance comes amid increased festive-season traction in the decorative paints segment. According to the company, all decorative paint categories witnessed strong demand ahead of the festive season. It also continued to report market share gains across its businesses.

Industrial paints performance was supported by demand from the infrastructure and energy sectors. In automotive coatings, the company reported customer wins and expansion into new verticals, strengthening its presence in the segment.

Despite revenue growth, profitability remained under pressure from elevated raw material costs. Comparable EBITDA from operations rose 4.4 per cent to Rs 110.9 crore from Rs 106.3 crore in the year-ago quarter. Profit after tax (PAT), excluding exceptional items, increased 2 per cent to Rs 71.2 crore.

Rajiv Rajgopal, Joint Managing Director and CEO, JSW Dulux, says, “We delivered consecutive quarter of double-digit volume and value growth, reflecting steady progress on our strategic priorities. We continued to make steady market share gains across our businesses. In Decorative Paints, all categories witnessed strong traction leading up to the festive season. Industrial Paints performance was aided by strong demand in infrastructure and energy sectors. We saw gains in automotive space with customer wins and entry into new verticals.”

He adds that the company has undertaken calibrated price increases to partly offset the impact of raw material inflation. “Despite these headwinds, comparable EBITDA grew 4.4 percent through prudent balance between cost management and growth initiatives. However, as geopolitical disturbances continue to affect raw material inflation, we will keep evaluating the situation and implementing calibrated price increases.”

For the first half of FY27, revenue from operations increased 20 per cent to Rs 1,926.9 crore on a comparable retained-business basis, while volume growth stood at 23 per cent. EBITDA from operations rose 9.4 per cent to Rs 226 crore, and PAT excluding exceptional items increased 50.5 per cent to Rs 206.7 crore. The first-half PAT includes dividend income of Rs 55.9 crore from the company’s subsidiary, ICI India Research and Technology Centre.

On the product front, the company launched VT Soft Sheen across India under its Accessible Luxury portfolio, combining its TruColour proposition with an eight-year Dulux Assurance warranty. Its Automotive and Specialty Coatings business also introduced the EONIX Rubbing and Polishing Compound range, expanding into adjacent categories within original equipment manufacturer-authorised workshop networks.

The company said elevated raw material inflation and geopolitical developments remain key factors influencing its pricing decisions and margins as it moves through the remainder of the financial year.
